summary: TechCrunch reports on Thanksgiving 2023 online sales, which grew only modestly: Adobe Analytics measured $5.6B in US online spending (+5.5%), while Salesforce put global online sales at $31.7B (+1%). Mobile set records and discounts drove spending, rather than inflation or buying pricier goods. Adobe forecasts $37.2B for the five-day Cyber Weekend, with Black Friday at $9.6B.
one_line: Thanksgiving 2023 online sales rose only modestly, with Adobe reporting $5.6B in the US and Salesforce $31.7B globally, driven by record mobile spending and deeper discounts.
key_facts: Adobe Analytics said US consumers spent $5.6 billion online on Thanksgiving 2023, up 5.5% on last year.
Salesforce reported global online sales of $31.7 billion on Thanksgiving, with a US tally of $7.5 billion, both up only 1%.
Salesforce said global average order value rose 2% to $103 per basket, while the US rose 1% to $119.
Adobe said $3.3 billion was spent on mobile devices on Thanksgiving, up 14% and an all-time record for the day.
Adobe predicts $37.2 billion in online spend over the five-day Cyber Weekend, up 5.4% year on year and 16.8% of all holiday spend.
Adobe forecasts Black Friday online sales of $9.6 billion, up 5.7%; the published 2022 figure was $9.13 billion.
Last year's Thanksgiving figure from Adobe was $5.29 billion; this year's 5.5% growth beats last year's 2.9% but is far below pre-COVID growth such as 18% or more in 2017.
Discounts in the US were up about 28% per both Adobe and Salesforce; toys and electronics saw sales up 182% and 113% over last month.
Mobile accounted for 59% of all online sales in the evening hours, per Adobe, while desktop still leads in conversions and items purchased.
Salesforce said mobile made up 79% of global online traffic and 82% in the US; Apple Pay transactions rose 47% versus 44% for all mobile wallets.
Social platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat accounted for 13% of all traffic referrals to sites but are mostly not where purchases happen.
Buy Now Pay Later drove $390 million in online spend, up 7.5% on last year, per Adobe.
Adobe's figures draw on 1 trillion visits to US retail sites, 100 million SKUs and 18 product categories; Salesforce uses data from 1.5 billion consumers.
